title: Kinematics (1D & 2D)
subject: physics
description: The description of motion — position, velocity and acceleration — without reference to its cause. The kinematic equations hold for constant acceleration.

title: Projectile Motion
subject: physics
description: Motion under gravity alone after launch. Horizontal velocity is constant; vertical motion is uniformly accelerated at g.

title: Newton's Laws of Motion
subject: physics
description: The three laws linking force and motion: inertia, F = ma, and action–reaction. The foundation of classical dynamics.

title: Friction
subject: physics
description: The contact force opposing relative sliding (kinetic) or the tendency to slide (static). Static friction is self-adjusting up to a maximum.

title: Work, Energy & Power
subject: physics
description: Work transfers energy; the work–energy theorem links net work to change in kinetic energy. Conservative forces define potential energy.

title: Momentum & Collisions
subject: physics
description: Linear momentum is conserved for an isolated system. Collisions are elastic (KE conserved) or inelastic (KE lost); impulse changes momentum.

title: Uniform Circular Motion
subject: physics
description: Motion on a circular path at constant speed requires a centripetal force directed toward the centre, continuously changing the velocity's direction.

title: Gravitation
subject: physics
description: Every mass attracts every other with a force along the line joining them. Governs orbits, tides and the structure of the cosmos.

title: Rotational Dynamics
subject: physics
description: The rotational analogue of translation: torque produces angular acceleration through the moment of inertia; angular momentum is conserved without external torque.

title: Simple Harmonic Motion
subject: physics
description: Oscillation where restoring force is proportional to displacement and directed toward equilibrium, giving sinusoidal motion with a fixed period.

title: Fluid Mechanics
subject: physics
description: Statics and dynamics of fluids: pressure, buoyancy, and the conservation of mass and energy in flow (continuity and Bernoulli).

title: Elasticity & Stress
subject: physics
description: How solids deform under load and recover. Within the elastic limit, stress is proportional to strain (Hooke's law for materials).

title: Wave Motion
subject: physics
description: A wave transfers energy and momentum through a medium (or field) without net transport of matter. Transverse vs longitudinal.

title: Superposition & Interference
subject: physics
description: Overlapping waves add displacement-by-displacement. Coherent sources produce stable constructive and destructive interference patterns.

title: Standing Waves & Resonance
subject: physics
description: Two identical waves travelling in opposite directions form a stationary pattern of nodes and antinodes — the basis of musical instruments.

title: Doppler Effect
subject: physics
description: The change in observed frequency when source and observer move relative to each other — heard in passing sirens, seen as redshift in galaxies.

title: Sound & Intensity Level
subject: physics
description: Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave. Loudness is perceived on a logarithmic decibel scale of intensity.

title: Beats
subject: physics
description: Two waves of slightly different frequency superpose to give a slow periodic rise and fall in loudness at the beat frequency.

title: Temperature & Heat
subject: physics
description: Temperature measures average molecular kinetic energy; heat is energy transferred due to a temperature difference. The zeroth law defines thermal equilibrium.

title: Kinetic Theory of Gases
subject: physics
description: Gases are many tiny particles in random motion; macroscopic pressure and temperature emerge statistically from molecular collisions.

title: First Law of Thermodynamics
subject: physics
description: Energy conservation for thermal systems: heat added to a system goes into internal energy and work done by the system.

title: Second Law & Entropy
subject: physics
description: Heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold; total entropy of an isolated system never decreases. Sets the arrow of time and limits engines.

title: Heat Engines & Carnot
subject: physics
description: A heat engine converts thermal energy into work by operating between a hot and cold reservoir. The Carnot cycle sets the maximum possible efficiency.

title: Thermal Expansion
subject: physics
description: Most materials expand when heated as atoms vibrate with larger amplitude. Quantified by linear, area and volume expansion coefficients.

title: Heat Transfer
subject: physics
description: Three mechanisms move thermal energy: conduction through contact, convection by fluid motion, and radiation by electromagnetic waves.

title: Reflection & Mirrors
subject: physics
description: Light bounces off surfaces with the angle of reflection equal to the angle of incidence. Curved mirrors form images governed by the mirror equation.

title: Refraction & Snell's Law
subject: physics
description: Light bends when changing medium because its speed changes. Snell's law relates the angles to refractive indices.

title: Thin Lenses
subject: physics
description: Lenses refract light to form images. The lens equation and ray diagrams predict image position, size and nature.

title: Young's Double Slit
subject: physics
description: Two coherent slits create alternating bright and dark fringes — the classic demonstration of the wave nature of light.

title: Diffraction
subject: physics
description: Waves bend around obstacles and spread through apertures. Diffraction sets the ultimate resolution limit of optical instruments.

title: Polarization
subject: physics
description: Light is a transverse wave, so its electric field can be restricted to one plane. Only transverse waves can be polarized.

title: Optical Instruments
subject: physics
description: Microscopes, telescopes and the eye combine lenses to magnify or resolve. Angular magnification is the key performance measure.

title: Electric Charge
subject: physics
description: Charge is a conserved, quantized property of matter. Like charges repel, unlike attract — the origin of all electrical phenomena.

title: Coulomb's Law
subject: physics
description: The electrostatic force between two point charges varies inversely with the square of their separation — analogous in form to gravitation.

title: Electric Field
subject: physics
description: A charge creates a field that exerts force on other charges. Field lines visualize direction and strength.

title: Electric Potential
subject: physics
description: Potential is the electrostatic potential energy per unit charge. Differences in potential drive currents and store energy.

title: Capacitance
subject: physics
description: A capacitor stores charge and energy in the electric field between conductors. Central to electronics and energy storage.

title: Gauss's Law
subject: physics
description: The electric flux through a closed surface equals the enclosed charge divided by ε₀ — a powerful shortcut for symmetric charge distributions.

title: Dielectrics & Polarization
subject: physics
description: Insulators polarize in a field, reducing the net field inside and increasing capacitance. Quantified by the dielectric constant.

title: Ohm's Law & Resistance
subject: physics
description: For ohmic conductors, current is proportional to voltage. Resistance opposes flow and depends on material and geometry.

title: Resistor Networks
subject: physics
description: Resistors combine in series and parallel; complex circuits reduce step-by-step or yield to Kirchhoff's laws.

title: Kirchhoff's Laws
subject: physics
description: Two rules from conservation of charge and energy that solve any circuit: the junction rule and the loop rule.

title: Electrical Power & Energy
subject: physics
description: Electrical energy converts to heat, light or work. Power is the rate of energy transfer in a circuit.

title: EMF & Internal Resistance
subject: physics
description: A real cell has internal resistance, so its terminal voltage drops under load below its EMF.

title: RC Circuits
subject: physics
description: Charging and discharging a capacitor through a resistor gives exponential time behaviour set by the time constant.

title: Magnetic Fields & Force
subject: physics
description: Moving charges and currents create magnetic fields and feel magnetic forces. The force is perpendicular to both velocity and field.

title: Biot–Savart & Ampère
subject: physics
description: Two laws give the magnetic field of currents: Biot–Savart for any element, Ampère's law for symmetric configurations.

title: Electromagnetic Induction
subject: physics
description: A changing magnetic flux induces an EMF (Faraday); the induced current opposes the change (Lenz) — the principle behind generators.

title: Inductance
subject: physics
description: An inductor opposes changes in current by storing energy in its magnetic field; mutual inductance couples two coils.

title: Alternating Current
subject: physics
description: AC voltage and current vary sinusoidally. Reactance, impedance and resonance govern AC circuit behaviour.

title: Transformers
subject: physics
description: Transformers change AC voltage via mutual induction between coils sharing an iron core, conserving power ideally.

title: Electromagnetic Waves
subject: physics
description: Oscillating electric and magnetic fields propagate as waves at the speed of light, spanning the EM spectrum from radio to gamma.

title: Photoelectric Effect
subject: physics
description: Light ejects electrons from a metal only above a threshold frequency — evidence that light is quantized into photons.

title: Bohr Model of the Atom
subject: physics
description: Electrons orbit the nucleus only in quantized energy levels; jumps between levels emit or absorb photons of definite energy.

title: Matter Waves (de Broglie)
subject: physics
description: Every particle has an associated wavelength; matter shows wave behaviour, confirmed by electron diffraction.

title: Heisenberg Uncertainty
subject: physics
description: There is a fundamental limit on simultaneously knowing complementary quantities such as position and momentum.

title: Atomic Spectra & X-rays
subject: physics
description: Atoms emit and absorb characteristic wavelengths; X-rays arise from inner-shell transitions and rapid electron deceleration.

title: Wavefunction & Schrödinger
subject: physics
description: A quantum system is described by a wavefunction whose squared magnitude gives the probability of finding the particle. It evolves via the Schrödinger equation.

title: Quantum Tunnelling
subject: physics
description: A particle can pass through a potential barrier it classically could not surmount — because its wavefunction extends into and beyond the barrier.

title: Radioactivity & Decay
subject: physics
description: Unstable nuclei spontaneously emit radiation (α, β, γ), decaying exponentially with a characteristic half-life.

title: Nuclear Binding Energy
subject: physics
description: The mass of a nucleus is less than its parts; the missing mass is the binding energy that holds it together (mass–energy equivalence).

title: Fission & Fusion
subject: physics
description: Splitting heavy nuclei (fission) or joining light ones (fusion) converts mass to energy — powering reactors, bombs and stars.

title: Particle Physics (Standard Model)
subject: physics
description: All matter is built from quarks and leptons interacting via force-carrying bosons. The Standard Model is our best theory of fundamental particles.

title: Special Relativity
subject: physics
description: At speeds near light, space and time are relative. The laws of physics and the speed of light are the same for all inertial observers.

title: Mass–Energy & Relativistic Momentum
subject: physics
description: Mass is a form of energy; momentum and energy take relativistic forms that reduce to Newtonian ones at low speed.

title: General Relativity (Intro)
subject: physics
description: Gravity is the curvature of spacetime by mass and energy. Massive objects bend the paths of light and slow time.

title: Stellar Physics
subject: physics
description: Stars are self-gravitating fusion reactors balancing gravity against outward gas pressure; their fate depends on mass.

title: Black Holes
subject: physics
description: A region where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape past the event horizon.

title: Cosmology & the Big Bang
subject: physics
description: The universe is expanding from a hot, dense beginning ~13.8 billion years ago, leaving observable relics like the cosmic microwave background.

title: Centre of Mass
subject: physics
description: The mass-weighted average position of a system. External forces move the centre of mass as if all mass were concentrated there.

title: Drag & Terminal Velocity
subject: physics
description: As a falling body speeds up, drag grows until it balances gravity — the body then falls at a constant terminal velocity.

title: Resonance & Forced Oscillation
subject: physics
description: When a driving frequency matches a system's natural frequency, energy transfer peaks and amplitude grows dramatically.

title: Damped Oscillation
subject: physics
description: Real oscillators lose energy to friction, so their amplitude decays exponentially over time.

title: Degrees of Freedom & Cv
subject: physics
description: Each independent way a molecule can store energy carries ½kT — fixing a gas's internal energy and heat capacities.

title: Maxwell–Boltzmann Distribution
subject: physics
description: In a gas, molecular speeds follow a characteristic distribution that broadens and shifts to higher speeds as temperature rises.

title: Dispersion & Prisms
subject: physics
description: Refractive index depends on wavelength, so a prism bends violet more than red — splitting white light into a spectrum.

title: The Human Eye & Defects
subject: physics
description: The eye focuses light onto the retina by changing its lens shape — and common defects are corrected with simple lenses.

title: Electric Dipole
subject: physics
description: Two equal and opposite charges a small distance apart — the basic model for polar molecules and antennas.

title: Van de Graaff & Breakdown
subject: physics
description: A moving belt carries charge onto a hollow sphere, building enormous potentials until the surrounding air breaks down.

title: Wheatstone Bridge
subject: physics
description: A four-resistor diamond that measures an unknown resistance precisely by balancing two voltage dividers.

title: Drift Velocity & Mobility
subject: physics
description: Electrons drift slowly through a conductor under an applied field, yet the current signal travels near light speed.

title: The Cyclotron
subject: physics
description: Charged particles spiral outward in a magnetic field, kicked to higher energy each half-turn by an alternating voltage.

title: LC Oscillations
subject: physics
description: Energy sloshes back and forth between a capacitor's electric field and an inductor's magnetic field — an electrical oscillator.

title: Lasers & Stimulated Emission
subject: physics
description: A laser produces an intense, coherent beam by stimulated emission — photons cloning themselves in a population-inverted medium.

title: Semiconductors & Diodes
subject: physics
description: Doping a pure semiconductor with impurities controls its conductivity — the basis of diodes, solar cells and all of modern electronics.

title: Radiocarbon Dating
subject: physics
description: Living things absorb carbon-14 at a steady rate; after death it decays with a known half-life, acting as a radioactive clock.

title: Quantum Entanglement
subject: physics
description: Two particles can share a single quantum state, so measuring one instantly determines the other — however far apart they are.

title: The Twin Paradox
subject: physics
description: A twin who travels near light speed and returns has aged less than the one who stayed — a real, measured consequence of relativity.

title: Gravitational Waves
subject: physics
description: Accelerating masses ripple spacetime itself; these waves travel at light speed and were finally detected from merging black holes.

title: Specific Heat of Water
subject: physics
description: Heating exactly 1 kg of water, the energy needed is Q = m·c·ΔT. Plot the energy you supply against the temperature rise — a straight line whose slope is the specific heat capacity c (since m = 1 kg).

title: Resistivity of a Wire
subject: physics
description: A uniform wire obeys R = ρL/A. Keeping the cross-section fixed at A = 1×10⁻⁷ m², plot resistance against length. The slope is ρ/A, so the resistivity ρ = slope × A.

title: Newton's 2nd Law — find a Mass
subject: physics
description: Newton’s second law says a = F/m. Pull a cart with measured forces and record its acceleration, then plot a against F. The slope is 1/m, so the mass m = 1 / slope.

title: Measure g with a Pendulum
subject: physics
description: A simple pendulum obeys T = 2π·√(L/g). Squaring: T² = (4π²/g)·L — a straight line whose slope is 4π²/g. Take T at several lengths, plot T² vs L, and the slope hands you g.

title: Hooke's Law — find a Spring Constant
subject: physics
description: A spring obeys F = k·x. Plot F (the load you hang) against the extension x it produces — a straight line through the origin whose slope is the spring constant k.

title: Ohm's Law — measure a Resistance
subject: physics
description: For an ohmic conductor, V = I·R. Vary the supply voltage, read the current, and plot V vs I. The graph is a straight line and its slope is the resistance R.

title: Wave Speed on a String
subject: physics
description: For a wave, v = f·λ, so λ = v·(1/f). Drive a string at several frequencies, measure the standing-wave wavelength, and plot λ vs 1/f — the slope is the wave speed v.

title: Refractive Index of a Medium
subject: physics
description: Snell's law: sin θ₁ = n·sin θ₂. Shine light into the glass at several angles, measure the refracted angle, and plot sin θ₁ against sin θ₂. The slope is the refractive index n.
